doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

chapter: Vibes, Bermuda and arriving in Canada
title: Why Canada: a girl, and hearing Red Norvo's trio at the Colonial Tavern
summary: He went to Canada after meeting a girl in Bermuda and there met Red Norvo, Tal Farlow and Mingus, going to hear the trio in Rochester.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well actually it was a girl I guess originally, that sort of got me up there. I met this girl in Bermuda and we got pretty serious. And she left and I went up to see her. And I liked the © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

country and I didn’t feel I was ready for New York, you know. And whilst I was up there to visit this girl, at the Colonial Tavern, which is a very famous jazz club there, Red Norvo was playing with his trio, with Tal Farlow and Charlie Mingus. And so I met him and they invited me to go down to Rochester with them. Mingus was out of it then. He said, “Drive me down in my Cadillac.” I said, “Are you kidding?” I said, “I’ve never driven here.” “Oh you can do it, get in my Cadillac and drive.” I said, “But I don’t have a driving license for this place. I’ve got one for Bermuda.” “Okay.” And I said, “No, no, I’ll come down on the bus.” So I went down on the bus. And they played this hotel which is similar to this one, in Rochester, and it was so great to hear that trio with Red. I mean he was a genius when it came to playing. It was incredible.

Norvo. Yeah. Four mallets. And his sound, you know, was so beautiful. He took — they had pulsators and the resonators you know, to give it a vibrato. He removed them. He wouldn’t use them. He got that flat, beautiful, crystal-like sound, yeah.
That was a trio without a drummer, wasn’t it?
That was, yeah, that was the trio, yeah.
And was it Tal Farlow or somebody, on guitar?
